prompt: Using the commuting table, what percent of the students who take the bus are in Grade $9$? Round to the nearest whole percent.
hint: "Of the students who take the bus" names the denominator.

hints.text: "Of the students who take the bus" names the denominator.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a two-by-two table: if $6$ of $10$ bus riders are in Grade 9, that is $60\%$ — denominator $10$, the bus total. The phrase after 'of' names the denominator.
The Bus row totals $80$, and $45$ of those are in Grade 9.

learningObjective: Compute a row-conditional percentage from a two-way table.
explanation: The phrase "of the students who take the bus" restricts the pool to the Bus row, total $80$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Row condition versus column condition
steps: This question conditions on a *row* (bus riders), so the row total is the denominator.
The earlier question conditioned on a *column* (Grade 10), so the column total was the denominator.
Same table, same numerator style, entirely different answers. Reading which way the condition runs is the whole skill.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: 45/110 ≈ 41% answers a different question — 'of Grade 9, what share ride the bus' — by conditioning on the column.
The phrase 'of the students who take the bus' names the ROW as the denominator: 45 of 80. Circle the denominator group before reading any number.
